hints.content:
$\displaystyle\lim_{x\to-\infty}g(x)$ represents the value $g$ approaches as $x$ becomes infinitely negative (i.e., as we move on the graph to the left).

$\displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}g(x)$ represents the value $g$ approaches as $x$ becomes infinitely positive (i.e., as we move on the graph to the right).

![The graph of function g has the first curve approaching the horizontal asymptote y = 4 as x approaches negative infinity. The second curve approaches the horizontal asymptote y = 1 as x approaches positive infinity.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/b72b066f49356d3e95e538a5b2639c645b8771d1)

$\displaystyle\lim_{x\to-\infty}g(x)$ seems to approach $4$ and $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}g(x)$ seems to approach $1$.

In conclusion, these are the limits of $g$ at negative and positive infinity:

$\begin{align}
&\displaystyle\lim_{x\to-\infty}g(x)=4
\\\\
&\displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}g(x)=1
\end{align}$
